title: The red-shift effect and radiation decay on black hole spacetimes
venue: Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics 62, 859-919 (2009); arXiv:gr-qc/0512119

verification.evidence: Abstract: 'We consider solutions to the linear wave equation on a (maximally extended) Schwarzschild spacetime ... We prove uniform decay bounds for the solution in the exterior regions ... We also prove uniform decay bounds for the flux of energy through the event horizon and null infinity. The estimates near the event horizon exploit an integral energy identity normalized to local observers. This estimate can be thought to quantify the celebrated red-shift effect.' Journal ref: Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 62 (2009), 859-919.

title: Critical phenomena in gravitational collapse

verification.evidence: Abstract: 'As first discovered by Choptuik, the black hole threshold in the space of initial data for general relativity shows both surprising structure and surprising simplicity. Universality, power-law scaling of the black hole mass, and scale echoing have given rise to the term critical phenomena. They are explained by the existence of exact solutions which are attractors within the black hole threshold, that is, attractors of codimension one in phase space, and which are typically self-similar. Critical phenomena give a natural route from smooth initial data to arbitrarily large curvatures visible from infinity, and are therefore likely to be relevant for cosmic censorship.' Journal ref: LivingRev.Rel.10:5,2007.

notes: Review; surfaced by the worker-09 L1 shard (W09-006). Used as the current numerical-status review for T-103, not as a theorem source.

title: Stability and instability of the sub-extremal Reissner-Nordstrom black hole interior for the Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon equations in spherical symmetry

verification.evidence: Abstract: 'We show non-linear stability and instability results in spherical symmetry for the interior of a charged black hole ... in presence of a massive and charged scalar field ... 1. Stability: ... sufficiently decaying polynomial decay rate on the event horizon gives rise to a space-time possessing a Cauchy horizon ... if the decay is even stronger, we prove that the spacetime metric admits a continuous extension to the Cauchy horizon. ... 2. Instability: ... the non-degenerate energy is infinite on any null surface crossing the Cauchy horizon and the curvature of a geodesic vector field blows up at the Cauchy horizon near time-like infinity. ... This instability ... can also be viewed as a step towards the resolution of the C^2 strong cosmic censorship conjecture for one-ended asymptotically initial data.' Related DOI: 10.1007/s00220-017-3079-3.

notes: EM-Klein-Gordon model; surfaced by the worker-09 L1 shard (W09-008). This is the correct model match for T-505 (unlike the EM-scalar Gautam paper).
